---
title: Setup
description: What you need before the session, and what to do if you do not have it.
---

The workshop runs in the browser. You install no software and you do no homework. You need three things.

| You need | Why | If you do not have it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A laptop with a current desktop browser | The GitHub interface hides parts of the menus on a phone. | Share a laptop with a neighbour. |
| A GitHub account | Every exercise creates something in your account. | Create one at the start (allow 10 minutes), or work in a pair. |
| Two-factor authentication that works on the day | GitHub asks for a second factor at sign-in. | Bring the device or the recovery codes that you use for GitHub. |

## Create a GitHub account

If you have no account yet, create it before the session if you can.

1. Open [github.com/signup](https://github.com/signup).
2. Use an e-mail address that you can open during the session.
3. Choose a username that you are comfortable to show in public. Your username appears on every repository and Issue.
4. Confirm the e-mail address.
5. Set up two-factor authentication when GitHub asks for it.

The free plan (GitHub Free) is sufficient. Students can also apply for [GitHub Education](https://education.github.com/), but the workshop does not need it.

## Choose your path

Before X1, decide how you work. You can change the decision later.

| Path | Who it is for | What changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Solo, public** | Default | Your exercise repository and Project are public. They contain only synthetic data. |
| **Solo, private** | You do not want public activity under your name. | Select **Private** for the repository and the Project. All exercises work the same way. |
| **Pair** | You have no account, or you prefer to work together. | One person owns the repository and adds the other as a collaborator. You review each other's pull requests in X4. |

::: {.callout-important}
## Synthetic data only

Do not put real personal data, unpublished research data, or third-party material into an exercise repository. The workshop gives you a synthetic dataset. For your real thesis, start with a **private** repository and a **private** Project. See [Transfer to a private thesis](solutions.qmd#private-thesis).
:::

## What to open on the day

- This website.
- The [template](https://github.com/maehr/open-research-data-template) that you start from in X1.
- The [showcase Project](https://github.com/users/maehr/projects/11) and the [example repository](https://github.com/maehr/projm-example-thesis), for comparison.
